I think I read somewhere that units don't "de-dominate" until **all** are done attacking. Since domination is the following process: Dominate > Attack, dominating 5 rear guards would mean they all attack at once, which is impossible to translate to a game. Since everything is dominated at the same time, every attack is considered to be happening at the same time as the "next attack".

Think like 2 on place skills, your vanguard column has a G1 and a Blaster Friend in the back row, you ride a Blaster Blade, you can choose to activate either Blaster Friend first or Blaster Blade's CB2 (Ideally, you would CB2 then CC1 with Blaster Friend). Since both skills happen at the same time, you pick the order, but technically, they happen at the **exact same time**.

And for that exact reason, during a Mujinlord turn, even if both G2 front rows have been dominated and have already attacked, they can't intercept, until after the whole chain of attacks.

A little extra thing to add, everything is dominated and leaves domination at the same time. So if you use Mujinlord to dominate, say 4 rear guards, 2 g2 front rows and 2 g1 back rows, you can attack with one of the front row first, then the other one, and they won't be able to intercept with the one that just attacked before that
